instructions:
# Hoppscotch

Test APIs with Hoppscotch in the browser and in CI with the CLI.

## What this skill does

- Runs exported collections headlessly in CI.
- Resolves environment variables across requests.
- Repeats iterations for smoke testing.
- Explains request chaining (values from previous responses).

## When to use

- Replaying a hand-crafted API session after an incident.
- Smoke testing an endpoint suite in CI without writing code.
- Sharing a reproducible request collection with the team.

## Real commands

```bash
# Install the CLI
npm install -g @hoppscotch/cli

# Run a collection (exported JSON from the Hoppscotch app)
hoppscotch run collection.json

# With an environment file
hoppscotch run collection.json -e prod.env.json

# Repeat N times
hoppscotch run collection.json --iteration 3

# Load env vars from .env (dotenv support)
npx @hoppscotch/cli run api-collection.json --dotenv .env
```

## Environment file

```json
{
  "name": "prod",
  "variables": [
    { "key": "baseUrl", "value": "https://api.example.com", "secret": false },
    { "key": "token", "value": "eyJ...", "secret": true }
  ]
}
```

## Testing

```bash
hoppscotch run collection.json -e prod.env.json --verbose
# exit code 0 when all requests in the collection succeed
```

## Best practices

- Keep collections exported from the workspace in git for CI replay.
- Mark secrets as secret in environments; never commit real tokens.
- Use environment files per stage (dev, staging, prod).
- Add test assertions in the collection so the CLI run fails on regressions.

## Example exchange

```
User: Run the checkout collection against prod.
Agent: hoppscotch run checkout-collection.json -e prod.env.json
```
